newsitem.title: USA: Developing countries reject veiled protectionism.
newsitem.headline: Developing countries reject veiled protectionism.

text.p: The G24 group of developing countries from Africa, Asia and Latin America will voice their objections to industrialized nations' veiled protectionist measures, according to a draft report.
The report obtained by Reuters was prepared for the Friday and Saturday meetings of delegates from the G24 as part of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

In the draft, the G24, which includes countries as diverse as India, Brazil and the Philippines, complained that Europe's unemployment problems are often blamed on trade liberalization, prompting pressure for protectionism.

"The advocacy of protectionism was particularly harmful when it was not even presented as such, but disguised under calls for environmental security, human rights or higher labor standards in the exporting countries," it said.

During the April meeting of the IMF and the World Bank the G24 voiced similar complaints after a report on the role of multilateral development banks that stressed a growing tendency to evaluate borrowers domestic policies.
The developing countries acknowledged the banks' efforts to help them reduce poverty, but they balked at the idea of lenders becoming sources of policy on domestic issues such as good governance.
